This game had been sitting in my Steam backlog for years. Getting a Steam Deck got me to give a whole bunch of games a second look and Dead Cells is now one of my best games of 2022. It has an amazingly engaging gameplay loop that makes it hard to put the game down. It has so much ways you can mix and match weapons and gadgets (of which there are probably over a hundred and they dramatically change your play style and breath infinite replayability in the game loop). As someone who tends to be attracted to the latest "triple A" (said with J.S. Sterling voice) games with flashy 3D graphics, it has revived my interest in pixelated side scrollers. If you have even the slightest of interest in this type of game, I highly recommend it.

Really hard but really good. You learn as you play, and the game more or less rewards you for failures - so even if you suck, you'll eventually progress...at least to a point. You will get your money's worth with this game.

This game is really good. My life was originally terrible but I saw dead cells on my steam library and decided to install it. After playing it for 6 hours, my life isn't terrible anymore. Dead Cells cures depression.

Every time you die you think "I can surely do better than that." and go straight back into a run. Death isn't a straight up punishment for you, it's simply an inspiration to do better.

Might literally be the pinnacle of the Roguelike genre. If you've never tried Roguelikes, this game will occupy your mind. If you don't like Roguelikes, this game will change your mind.

If you do plan on buying this game, the DLC is basically mandatory. The "Medley of Pain" bundle + the free Rise of the Giant DLC will get you all the content. It's worth the asking price but the game is fairly old at this point so wait for a sale.

Hard to articulate how I feel about this game. Two years ago, it was game of the year, and deservingly so. It was a finely crafted game that was the result of useful community feedback during early access.

However, since the official release, MT inexplicably treats the game as if it's still in early access, sometimes making arbitrary changes, sometimes making wholesale changes to core mechanics, and sometimes incorporating 'community suggestions' that make the game, in some respects, easier. Ironically, they then later respond to those same community tweaks by introducing artificial difficulty.

All that I wanted to play was the game that I originally purchased (which was labeled as an official release...not early access...) + any DLCs, and now I can't play that game anymore without sacrificing the new content as well. So... thanks... I guess.

The developers have really eroded my enthusiasm, and I regret talking so many people into purchasing this.

You've been warned: The game you're purchasing now might not be the game you're playing a year from now either.

It's clear the devs put a ton of effort into this game. It's polished, and has plenty of DLC content to enjoy as well. If you are into roguelikes, this is a must play. If you're not, or even if you downright dislike the genre like me, it's still a must play.

An Amazing gem of an 2D Action/Platformer. The Combat is nice and punchy, the sprites and graphics are nice and appealing, there is a deep amount of weapons and upgrades. The random castle generator works and isn't a tacky gimmick that doesn't work. The concept of flat out dying with no check-points and starting all over is intimidating and can seem frustrating at first, but after a few lives I was used to it and saw the beauty in that mechanic which makes this game unique.

My only problem with this game is the few bugs I have experienced, none being game breaking or extremely annoying.

If you're looking for a cheap, fun game to dump time into or if your a fan of dungeon crawling, hack n' slashers, this game is worth every penny.

Overall: 9/10

I've played 90 hours so far and I'm gonna be playing a lot more. I hope this helps someone out there, and thank you for reading this.

An absolute masterpiece of a game. I often think of that one quote in the steam trailer "Motion Twin thought of everything" and really that does describe it perfectly.
You're able to change the ENTIRE playstyle to your liking through countless playthrough options with little to no consequence.
Manoeuvrability is such a factor to me personally when it comes to platformer fighters, and this game goes beyond expectations, especially with the challenge of performance rewards after each level.
The soundtrack is possibly a third (to maybe a half) of the awesomeness to this game; with the mood matching the atmosphere and the intensity of the fights.
The DLCs are all worth getting (especially queen of the sea imo ;)) all for reasons listed previously, as well as the most fun and intense boss battles I've ever encountered in any 2d game overall.
Also probably the smoothest pixelated game animations I've ever seen
A great platformer, I waited until a discount was applied to it and took it with all the dls. Definitely have a collection for fans of platformers.

This is arguably the best 'Metroidvania' Game I've ever played. It's superior to Castlevania:SotN. It's superior to Super Metroid. It's the most addicting, mechanically sound Game of this Genre ever made. It's silly hard very quick. It's indepth. There are many different types of character you can be early on clear into late game. Want to be an upclose brawler? No problem. Distance sniper with 'eleventy' arrows at a time? Got it. Assassin with big flashy numbers that critically hit often? Done. The game is a joy to play, still in Early Access, but doesn't feel like EA at all. Do not sit on the fence with this one. It's a steal at the price it's at, and you're guaranteed hours and hours of enjoyment. Get it. Now.

Dead Cells is a rogue-lite that is easy to play but hard to master. It has a very high replay value due to the large amounts of items that there is. If you are someone who enjoys to spend time on a game to see improvements on your gameplay later on and finds joy in finishing difficult tasks, then this game is definitely for you.

Little did I know, that I was playing the new Castlevania without knowing. The french were training me to accept a new Dead Cells with another coat of paint.

Know what you are getting into:

Dead cells deserves all the praise it gets, it has great, tight controls and very challenging but fair gameplay. But if you are looking for a roguelike you can maximize in a few weeks, look elsewhere. Not only is dead cells challenging, but so many different weapons and items play so differently from each other that learning how to do everything in this game would take a very, very longgg time. And the game is updated fairly regularly, often significantly changing the gameplay. I've more or less beaten other roguelites like gungeon, rogue legacy, 20xx but I don't think I'll ever fully complete this game, lol. There's just wayyy to much to learn.

If you want a good metroidvania-like 2D action roguelike with great progression and a bunch of content, this is it.
The most important aspect of games like this, for me, is to have pixel perfect control of your character, and Dead Cells achieves this better than any other action roguelike that I know of.
There's certainly a lot of dying, but every time you can feel like you had control and know what you could've done to prevent it. Frustrating game that teaches you your limitations.

Some negatives is that, getting it now, there's a bunch of DLCs that you kind of want. You don't "need" them, and the game feels complete without them, but if you want it all, there's 4 DLCs to buy apart from the base game itself.
To clear the game requires to play on hardest setting. I failed to stupidity in my runs, but thankfully, there's an assist-mode that you can use and abuse to let you progress further, be it "continues", disabling traps, or simply making yourself invincible. All up to you.

I want to like this more than I think I do…it’s very slick and fun to play, but tuned so aggressively with difficulty that I am struggling to want to continue. For context, I have beaten most major Fromsoft games including Sekiro (which I love).

I was able to beat Dracula with assist mode only using infinite continues, and that still felt satisfying, but my desire to push farther and grind is minimal right now. I could turn on other assist mode options, but it doesn’t feel rewarding to do that. I would have liked to see 0BC tuned a little easier to onboard the player before it ramps up.

Make no mistake, most people disagree, and I may edit this review if it clicks in the future. But I think I’ve given this a fair shot and I’m not sure I want to keep pushing.

Dead Cells is awesome.

Roguelike metroivania with perfect run length, progression, lore, atmosphere, controls, music and graphics.

Most importantly, the action is GREAT. The weapons are mostly very satisfying to use and pack a real punch. Enemies are varied and have a whole lot of patterns to learn.

Difficulty starts out reasonably. It's challenging but not unfair or unforgiving. You'll unlock new difficulty levels by beating previous ones. The going gets hellish enough for even good players, or so I understand.

I find myself coming back to it time and time again, even though I know I'll never beat the harder difficulties, let alone see the "real ending".

This game broke me in ways few things on this planet ever could. I have been beaten by many people in my life, had exposed nerve endings inside my mouth and had allergic reactions that made it impossible to breath. YET STILL this game broke me more. Good thing Leghugger carried me.

Very addictive, fast game play. I like that each time you die, your character has made progress and comes back stronger and can tackle more levels and tougher enemies. Easy to pick up and put down, as runs are not usually more than an hour at a stretch.

Dead Cells is incredible.

I have played a lot of roguelites. Few manage to achieve the perfect balance between consistently exciting combat, meaningful progression, and choose-your-own playstyle that Motion Twin achieves with this masterpiece. I have seen most of what this game has to offer and, despite a growing backlog of games, I keep coming back to it. This is the ultimate test of the genre, and Dead Cells emphatically passes it.

It's strong in less important ways too that make it a complete package. The art style is tight--simple but pleasing. The world is mysterious and interesting, with lore that plays out through treasured snippets as you throw your body against it again and again. There is a dark foreboding lurking here, and the further you're willing to commit, the more the game shows you. It's rewarding in a brooding way many games attempt and few get right.

If you're into roguelites, metroidvania, or action/platforming in general, you cannot pass this game up. It is best-in-class.
best rouge like better so many unique combos and level design and enemy design so good game never gets old

While it doesn't have the full depth of either genre it combines, the devs compensated for it with competence and high quality in, well, pretty much every aspect of the game. There was not a single moment where I thought "uuh this is some bull­s­h­і­t" and had a lot of moments like "yeah this is nice and makes sense" instead.
This might sound a bit disappointing to people who were only interested in this for the roguelike part OR metroidvania part, but that's not the game's downside at all - it wasn't made for them.
As for the Early Access stuff: at the moment of writing the game is close to launch and I don't think I've encountered a single bug, and the game's balance seems to have been tweaked enough times for me to not have any complaints about it.

Another thing - after about 10 hours I've mostly lost interest in the game, despite there still being plenty of items left to discover. This might be due to me "peaking" in the game quite early / sooner than intended (in terms of level progression) coupled with ADHD, though, so it's not an objective indicator in any way. Again, not a bad thing: I'd rather have 10 hours of interesting and concentrated runs than the same amount of fun stretched over a 100.

This is an example of Metroidvania done correctly.
Controls are fast and responsive. The pixel art is beautiful and colorful.
The items variation are great.
At some point slightly repetitive. But unlocking new weapons and skills overrides the repetitiveness.
I put this and Hollow Knight on the top of new Metroidvania style games.

I played for two hours, and the first and a half was only to beat the first boss. I am bad at this game, but I like that I'm bad at this game.

I hate rogue-likes. I tried some and couldn't bring myself to play for more than a couple of hours before boredom.

Dead Cells changed that and I actually had fun dying again and again.

The amount of weapons and how to play is astonishing and I love that you could take multiple routes and come back to the first via teleportation. The game overall feels very impactful and gorey and I like that.

Try it out if you like rogue-likes or not, but it sure feels good when you kill stuff and progression is actually quite fast for a rogue-like. I thought it would need multiple amount of time to beat the first level but it was quite easy.

WouldDieAgainThankYou/10

I don't often write reviews but when I do, it turns out like this.
Best. Game. IN. A. While! I strongly recommend a controller - even if you need to get used to the feel, it will make the experience all the better.

Now, I was never a friend of grinding, but this game just does this right. It hooks you with new challenges, new areas, learning recipes, achieving powers, testing synergies of weapons, telling a subtle but fun story (there is a twist at the end, totally worth it!) and so much more.

If you want it tweaked, go to the workshop! It's all there - even harder versions!
